items.title: Seifert disk-and-band construction from an oriented knot diagram

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory, §3.2, pp.24–26
references.locator: Seifert's algorithm and its disk-and-band construction

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, §4.3, pp.21–23
references.locator: The all-at-once oriented smoothing and disk-and-band algorithm

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with exactly one component, and let $c$ be its number of crossings. Perform the following construction in its projection sphere $S^2$.

1. Choose a point $q\in S^2$ outside the finite diagram. In pairwise disjoint small disks about the crossings, replace each crossing by the unique noncrossing smoothing compatible with the strand orientations. Let the resulting oriented circles be the Seifert circles and let $s$ be their number.
2. For each Seifert circle $C$, take the closure of the component of $S^2\setminus C$ that does not contain $q$. Under the stated choice axiom, each such region is an embedded compact disk. The finite family of disk regions is nested or disjoint. Orient each disk to induce the given orientation of its boundary circle, then place nested disks at distinct nearby heights ordered by inclusion; the resulting disk interiors are pairwise disjoint in $S^3$.
3. For every original crossing, attach one rectangular band along short boundary intervals on the two smoothing arcs. A half-twist means a single $180$-degree turn of the band across the crossing neighborhood. Choose its direction, endpoint orientations, and over/under order to match the original crossing.
4. Return the finite disk-and-band construction data together with $(s,c)$.

The returned data are a finite attached two-dimensional complex. This algorithm's definition alone does not assert that the resulting image is embedded, is a surface, is connected, or has the original knot as boundary; the separate correctness lemma establishes those properties.

items.title: Oriented Seifert surfaces in the three-sphere

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory, §3.1, pp.21–22
references.locator: Definition 3.1; compact connected oriented spanning surfaces

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, §4.3, pp.21–23

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere $S^3$. A **Seifert surface** for $K$ is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F\subset S^3$ with boundary set equal to $K$. Orient each boundary component so that an outward-pointing conormal in $F$, followed by a positive boundary tangent, is a positive basis of $TF$; the oriented boundary of $F$ must agree with the given orientation of $K$. For such a surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the unique nonnegative integer satisfying $\chi(F)=2-2g(F)-b$, where $b$ is the number of boundary components; here $b=1$, so $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. The compact-surface normal-form result supplies this integer under the stated choice axiom.

items.title: Smooth Jordan disks and extension of prescribed boundary collars
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The bounded region of a smooth embedded
circle in the oriented plane, together with its boundary, is a smooth manifold
with boundary diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Let $D_0,D_1$ be two
such closed regions. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary
diffeomorphism $b:\partial D_0\to\partial D_1$ extends to an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $B:D_0\to D_1$. More precisely, for
specified smooth inward collars $c_i:\partial D_i\times[0,\epsilon)\to D_i$
with $c_i(p,0)=p$, the extension may be required to satisfy
$B(c_0(p,r))=c_1(b(p),r)$ for every sufficiently small $r\ge0$. In addition, given interior points $p_i\in D_i$ and an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $q$ from a neighborhood of $p_0$ onto a neighborhood of $p_1$, the extension can agree with $q$ near $p_0$ while retaining the prescribed boundary collars.

references.title: C. T. C. Wall, Differential Topology, Theorem 2.4.2 and Sections 2.6–2.7

items.statement: Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented three-sphere, and let $F$ be a connected compact oriented smooth embedded surface with oriented boundary $K$. Fix the standard round metric on $S^3$. A normal field along $K$ assigns to every point $p\in K$ a nonzero vector in the plane orthogonal to $T_pK$; two such fields represent the same framing class when they are homotopic through nonzero normal fields. The inward unit vector tangent to $F$ along $K$, together with the positive quarter-turn in each oriented normal plane, gives a reference frame. In this frame the relative normal field is a map $K\cong S^1\to S^1$, and its degree gives a bijection from framing classes to $\mathbb Z$. Adding $n$ positive full twists changes this integer by $n$.

items.title: Seifert disks and bands form an embedded oriented spanning surface

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a single knot, and let the Seifert algorithm supply its finite disk-and-band construction data. These disks and bands can be realized in $S^3$ as a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F$ with exactly one boundary component, whose oriented boundary is the knot represented by $D$. The bands can be chosen mutually disjoint and disjoint from disk interiors except at their attaching intervals.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular oriented diagram with exactly one component, the Seifert diagram procedure terminates after one finite smoothing scan and one finite band-record scan. It returns exactly one disk record for each Seifert circle and exactly one band record for each original crossing. Termination alone asserts no embeddedness, boundary equality, or genus minimality.

items.title: Seifert surfaces and smooth knot genus

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory, §3.1, pp.21–22
references.locator: Definition 3.1 and the note that existence is established by Seifert's algorithm

references.title: Alessia Cattabriga and Stefano Francaviglia, Knot Theory and Applications: Lecture Notes, §4.3, pp.21–23

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, define

$$\mathcal G(K):=\{n\in\mathbb N_0: \text{there is a Seifert surface }F\text{ for }K\text{ with }g(F)=n\}.$$

Every element of $\mathcal G(K)$ is the genus of a connected compact oriented surface. The existence theorem makes $\mathcal G(K)$ nonempty, and the well-ordering of $\mathbb N_0$ gives its least element. The **smooth knot genus** is $g(K):=\min\mathcal G(K)$. This genus is the minimum over embedded spanning surfaces; it is not the number of Seifert circles or the genus of every surface produced from a diagram.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If a connected compact oriented disk-and-band surface $F$ is built from $s$ disjoint disks by attaching $c$ rectangular bands along boundary intervals and has one boundary component, then $\chi(F)=s-c$ and $g(F)=(1-s+c)/2$. In particular, if the Seifert algorithm on an oriented knot diagram $D$ has $s$ Seifert circles and $c$ crossings, its output surface has genus $(1-s+c)/2$ and the knot genus satisfies $g(K)\le (1-s+c)/2$. This is an upper bound from one spanning surface, not a minimality assertion.

items.title: A Seifert framing has zero self-linking

references.locator: Linking number as signed intersection with a spanning surface

references.locator: Seifert zero framing, self-linking as a push-off linking number, and framing classes via SO(2)

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$. The normal framing along $K$ given by the inward unit conormal to $K$ in $F$ has self-linking number zero. Here self-linking is the linking number of $K$ with a sufficiently small disjoint push-off along that framing. In the framing-class parameterization by relative winding from the surface framing, this class has integer zero.
